report.summary:
Here's what I've learned about you. Southside Youth Peace Collective started in 2023 and is now in its third year. You do street outreach and youth mentoring with a team of four, and two of you work full time. Young people and families trust you. That trust is your greatest asset, and it is hard to build. Much of the behind-the-scenes work runs through you and your founder. Your funding comes from one city contract plus small individual gifts.

You are strong in the basics that many young groups skip. Your answers show you use an accounting system, you share financial duties, and you build an annual budget. You track who you serve and what services you deliver, and someone on your team is responsible for data. You also have supporters who give, you have won grants of $10,000 or more, and you know where your money comes from for the next 6 to 12 months. That is a real base to build on.

You have room to grow in four areas. They are writing down your plans, making sure payroll is steady, getting funding that lasts more than one year, and defining the changes you want to see in young people. Your answers put all four areas at the Seeding stage. That is normal for a group in year three that has put its energy into the block, not paperwork. These are growth priorities, not failures.

If I were you, I would start with two things. First, write one short work plan that says what you will do, by when, and who owns each task. Second, look closely at your cash flow so payroll is safe, especially with one city contract carrying so much weight. Both are small enough for one person to do. They also give funders and your city contact proof that you are steady. The rest can wait until these are in place.

Esto es lo que he aprendido sobre usted: lidera un grupo de barrio que nació en 2023 y que ya va en su tercer año. Hace interrupción de violencia y mentoría para jóvenes. Su mayor tesoro es la confianza que tienen los jóvenes y las familias en su equipo. Con 4 personas (2 de tiempo completo) y un presupuesto de unos $310K, gran parte del trabajo de oficina pasa por usted y por el fundador. Eso es mucha carga para pocas manos. Este informe es una herramienta para aprender, no una evaluación.

Usted es fuerte en varias cosas que no todos los grupos jóvenes tienen. Ya usa un sistema de contabilidad, reparte las responsabilidades del dinero y arma un presupuesto anual. Lleva registro de las actividades básicas y de las personas que atiende, y tiene a alguien con tiempo para los datos. También sabe de dónde vendrá el dinero en los próximos 6 a 12 meses y ha conseguido subvenciones de $10,000 o más. Sus respuestas muestran que las cuatro áreas revisadas (planificación, recaudación de fondos, manejo del dinero y aprendizaje con datos) están hoy en la etapa Semilla. Es lo normal para un grupo en sus primeros años, y hay una base real sobre la cual construir.

Usted tiene espacio para crecer en poner por escrito lo que ya sabe hacer: un plan de trabajo, metas que todo el equipo pueda explicar y resultados que usted quiera medir. También en tener más claridad sobre el flujo de dinero y en depender menos de un solo contrato de la ciudad. Si yo fuera usted, empezaría con dos cosas. Primero, un plan de trabajo sencillo de una página. Segundo, una mirada clara a cuándo entra y cuándo sale el dinero, para pagar la nómina con tranquilidad. Estas dos bases abren la puerta a conseguir fondos de varios años y hacen que el trabajo dependa menos de una sola persona. El resto lo iremos haciendo en 90 días, paso a paso.

report.summary:
Here's what I've learned about you. Riverbend has been at this work since 2016. You run hospital-based intervention and street outreach with 19 staff and a budget of about $2.1 million. Your answers show that core systems exist and your team uses them, but they work better in some places than others. Your board is up and running, though it has few people with finance skills. Most of your money, roughly 80%, comes from restricted government funding. Restricted means it can only be spent in set ways.

You are strong in planning. Your answers show written work plans that you update and check often, and a written fundraising plan. You are also strong in money management. You review financial reports with leaders and the board, and you do an independent audit each year. In learning and evaluation, you set outcomes, track them, review data as a team and share results with funders and partners. Your planning and money management are at the Developing stage, which means the habits are in place and are growing.

You have room to grow in fundraising and in learning from your data. Both are at the Emerging stage. You also have room to grow in how your whole team collects data in the same way, and in how clearly you can see your funding over the next year. When most of your money is restricted, one late or lost grant can shake the whole team. Better data also helps you tell your story to funders.

If I were you, I would start with two things. First, build a clear, written picture of where your money will come from over the next 12 months. Second, help every staff member collect data the same way. The first protects your staff and participants. The second makes your numbers solid enough to win bigger and longer grants. Everything else can follow in small steps over the next 90 days.
